title: What a ZPA Microsegmentation Flow log record says and does not say

prose.text: The Microsegmentation Flow log is generated by Microsegmentation agents and describes network flows with a policy decision. Its enforcement fields have value lists but no documented combinations.

prose.label: Enforcement.
prose.text: {{enforcement-enums}} {{enforcement-descriptions}} The combinations are open {{gap:enforcement-triple}}. Reading blocks as lateral movement is not sourced {{gap:lateral-movement-reading}}.

checks.do: Whether a SIEM rule for blocked flows relies on one enforcement field alone, given the combinations are undocumented.
Whether SourcePorts, AppName and AppExecutablePath are parsed as arrays.

agent-generated-aggregated.statement: A flow record comes from a Microsegmentation agent: ResourceID, ResourceName and AppZone fields describe the agent generating the flow log, and ConnectionStartTime is the timestamp when the earliest of an aggregated set of connections was initiated.

quotes: | ResourceID | The resource ID associated with the agent generating the flow log
| ConnectionStartTime | The timestamp when the earliest of an aggregated set of connections was initiated

source-ports-aggregated.statement: SourcePorts is the source port of the connection, and for multiple connections between the same endpoints (same source, destination address, protocol and destination port) it becomes an aggregated source port list.

quotes: In the case of multiple connections between the same endpoints (i.e., same source, destination address, protocol, and destination port), this becomes an aggregated source port list.

array-valued-sample.statement: In the example record SourcePorts, AppName and AppExecutablePath are JSON arrays, although AppName and AppExecutablePath are described as a single application name and path.

enforcement-enums.statement: EnforcementReason allows POLICY_DISABLED, RULE, NO_POLICY_EXISTS and FORCED; EnforcementAction allows ALLOW, BLOCK and SIMBLOCK; EnforcementDisposition allows UNKNOWN, CONNECTED, REJECTED and DROPPED; and Direction allows UNKNOWN, INBOUND and OUTBOUND.

enforcement-descriptions.statement: EnforcementReason is described as the policy enforcement configured on the connection, EnforcementAction as the policy enforcement action configured on the connection, and EnforcementDisposition as the policy enforcement decision on the connection.

quotes: | EnforcementReason | The policy enforcement configured on the connection
| EnforcementAction | The policy enforcement action configured on the connection
| EnforcementDisposition | The policy enforcement decision on the connection

protocol-numeric.statement: Protocol is the transport protocol used in the connection with a numeric specifier, and the example record has Protocol 6 and DestinationPort 1443 as numbers.

quotes: | Protocol | The transport protocol used in the connection | %[OPT]d |

enforcement-triple.title: What combinations of EnforcementReason, EnforcementAction and EnforcementDisposition mean
enforcement-triple.blocks: filtering for flows that were actually blocked versus flows that would be blocked
enforcement-triple.detail: Unverified legacy statement (ledger log-18): each of the three fields has an allowed-value list (enforcement-enums) but the combinations are not documented. Open combinations include POLICY_DISABLED with BLOCK and CONNECTED (a monitor-mode block that was allowed?), NO_POLICY_EXISTS with DROPPED (an implicit deny or an unrelated drop?), SIMBLOCK with CONNECTED, REJECTED or DROPPED, and what UNKNOWN disposition means. Also open: whether aggregated connections must share one EnforcementAction or can mix dispositions in one record (source-ports-aggregated). The legacy also states SIMBLOCK flows are connections that would be blocked in enforcement mode but are only simulated, a reading the captures do not give. Unverified legacy statement: POLICY_DISABLED means the policy exists but is in monitor mode, RULE that a specific rule matched, NO_POLICY_EXISTS that no applicable policy was found, and FORCED that enforcement was forced regardless of rules; the disposition CONNECTED means allowed, REJECTED that a TCP reset was sent, and DROPPED that the flow was silently dropped. No capture gives these meanings.

lateral-movement-reading.title: Reading blocked east-west flows as lateral movement
lateral-movement-reading.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Microsegmentation Flow logs record lateral movement and east-west traffic between workloads, and many blocked attempts to one DestinationPort from several sources inside one AppZone may indicate lateral movement, a misconfigured application or an over-restrictive policy. The capture calls the log network flow information from agents and gives no such reading.
